full_text_en:
Niutuozhi Village v. China Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Temporary Land Use

Plaintiff (Appellant at Second Instance): Niutuozhi Village Committee, Yonghong Township, Xijiao District, Tianjin.
Legal Representative: Niu Xingcai, Director of Niutuozhi Village Committee.
Agent ad litem at First and Second Instances: Zhang Caizhen, Lawyer, Xijiao District Legal Advisory Office, Tianjin; Niu Shengli, Farmer of Niutuozhi Village.

Defendant (Appellee at Second Instance): China Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Sino-Japanese joint venture).
Legal Representative: Nie Yuhe, Manager of China Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem at First and Second Instances: Wang Ruxian, Section Chief of Engineering Affairs, China Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem at First Instance: Wang Tianju, Lawyer, Tianjin No. 1 Legal Advisory Office.
Agent ad litem at Second Instance: Zhao Guangyu, Lawyer, Tianjin Economic and Technological Development Zone Legal Advisory Office.

The plaintiff, Niutuozhi Village Committee, filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, China Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., concerning a dispute over a temporary land use contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant, due to construction needs, temporarily borrowed 16.036 mu (approximately 1.07 hectares) of arable land owned by the plaintiff adjacent to the east of the defendant's factory. During negotiations for borrowing the land, the plaintiff repeatedly stated that after the defendant finished using the land, it must be properly cleared, not even a single brick left, so that it could be directly cultivated upon return. After the contract was printed, the plaintiff discovered that the clause regarding the return of the land did not include the restoration of cultivation conditions, and thus requested a modification of the contract. At that time, the defendant's responsible person readily agreed and asked the plaintiff to affix its seal first. Relying on mutual trust, the plaintiff affixed its seal to the contract. Unexpectedly, the defendant intentionally reversed the positions of Party A and Party B, imposing its own obligations onto the plaintiff. Due to the plaintiff's negligence, it did not personally review the modified contract, but only listened to the defendant's reading and affixed its seal again without careful consideration. The defendant thereby deceived the plaintiff. As the defendant had dug trenches on the borrowed land, laid foundations with lime and cement, poured concrete floors for indoor areas and a basketball court, bricks were scattered everywhere, and the soil quality was severely damaged. Although the borrowed land has been vacated by the defendant, it remains uncultivable. Therefore, the plaintiff requests the defendant to restore the borrowed land to cultivable condition and compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 60,138.

Defendant's Defense: During the borrowing of the land, there were multiple negotiations regarding the amount of borrowing fees and the responsibility for land clearance. When discussing the restoration of the land's appearance, the defendant, considering the possibility of differing views on what constitutes cultivable condition, proposed that after use, the defendant would be responsible for demolishing all structures down to the indoor floor level, while the plaintiff would be responsible for restoring the land to cultivable condition. The costs for this could be resolved by increasing the usage fee as a lump sum. The amount of the usage fee was further negotiated several times, and finally the defendant agreed to increase the annual usage fee from RMB 600 per mu to RMB 1,500 per mu, to which the plaintiff agreed. Accordingly, the contract was signed. As for the plaintiff's allegation that when affixing seals, it requested contract modifications and the defendant readily agreed, and that the modified contract was only read aloud once by the defendant without the plaintiff's review before sealing, this is entirely fabricated. The defendant believes that once a contract is signed and sealed, it has legal effect. The defendant has fully completed all its obligations regarding the use of the land, and there are no remaining issues.

Facts Found by the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court: During the construction of its factory buildings, in order to solve the living base for construction personnel, the defendant entered into a temporary land use contract with the plaintiff on October 10, 1981. The contract stipulated that the plaintiff would lend 16.036 mu of land adjacent to the defendant's factory to the defendant for temporary use, with a term from October 1981 to December 1983. If construction was not completed by the expiration date, the contract would continue to be effective. The land use fee was RMB 1,500 per mu per year; less than half a year would be counted as half a year, and less than one year would be counted as one year. The contract was approved by the Xijiao District urban construction department on November 5 of the same year. Subsequently, when the defendant supplemented the content after Article 4, Paragraph 2 of the contract with the clause "matters concerning restoring the land to cultivable condition, etc., shall be the responsibility of Party A (the plaintiff)," both parties affixed their seals to confirm, and it was also recognized by the Xijiao District urban construction department. On November 9 of the same year, the defendant delivered the borrowed land to the construction unit for use. During the period of use, the defendant paid the plaintiff a land use fee of RMB 72,162 in accordance with the contract. On October 19 of the same year, the defendant separately entered into another contract with the construction unit (a third party), which included the clause that upon completion of construction, when the construction unit "withdraws, it shall demolish all buildings down to the indoor floor level and remove all demolition debris and above-ground objects from the site." In March 1984, when the defendant's construction was completed and the construction unit withdrew, it sold the temporary housing it had built to the plaintiff for RMB 10,000. Consequently, on March 21, 1984, the plaintiff entered into another agreement with the third party, with the third party as Party A and the plaintiff as Party B. The agreement stipulated: "After Party A withdraws, all temporary buildings within the scope of this agreement shall be demolished by Party B down to the indoor floor level (i.e., bounded by the cement floor), and Party B shall be responsible for the removal and transportation of discarded bricks and soil (including the discarded bricks and soil from tents already removed by the construction unit)." Subsequently, the plaintiff demanded that the defendant restore the borrowed land to cultivable condition. The defendant insisted on performing the contract as agreed.

Opinion of the Tianjin Intermediate People's Court: The plaintiff alleged that the defendant intentionally reversed the obligations of the two parties and deceived the plaintiff. However, the plaintiff admitted that the defendant had read aloud to it the clause "matters concerning restoring the land to cultivable condition, etc., shall be the responsibility of Party A," and that it had affixed its seal; it also admitted that it held a copy of the contract text. Moreover, the plaintiff failed to provide any evidence to prove it was deceived; therefore, its claim was untenable. The contract signed by both parties is lawful and valid. The contract stipulated that the defendant's obligation to demolish all buildings down to the indoor floor level had been transferred to the third-party construction unit, and the separate agreement between the plaintiff and the third-party construction unit clearly provided that this obligation was assumed by the plaintiff itself. The plaintiff's request for the defendant to immediately restore the borrowed land to cultivable condition and compensate for losses of over RMB 60,000 was unreasonable and was not supported. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Measures for Land Acquisition for National Construction, the court rendered the following judgment on June 20, 1986: (1) The construction temporary land use contract signed by both parties is a valid contract; (2) The plaintiff's claims are dismissed. Court acceptance fee of RMB 580.81 shall be borne by the plaintiff.

The plaintiff, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Tianjin High People's Court on the grounds that the contract was illegal and manifestly unfair, and that the original judgment was erroneous.

Opinion of the Tianjin High People's Court upon review: Regarding the legality of the contract, upon investigation, Article 12 of the Measures for Land Acquisition for National Construction promulgated by the State Council in 1958 provides that for temporary construction land use, the parties shall enter into an agreement, which shall be approved by the local government, and the land user shall provide appropriate compensation for losses caused to the landowner. The contract and its supplement signed by both parties were negotiated by mutual agreement, signed and sealed by both parties, and approved and recognized by the relevant urban construction department. Therefore, the contract is lawful and valid. Regarding whether the contract was manifestly unfair, upon verification, the land use fee stipulated in the contract was RMB 1,500 per mu per year. The appellee used the land for approximately three years and paid the appellant RMB 72,162. The total costs required for the appellant to clear the site and restore the land to cultivable condition, plus the actual losses from lending out the land for three years, amounted to over RMB 53,400. The appellee had fully compensated the appellant's actual losses, and there was no unfairness. The appellant's request for the appellee to restore the borrowed land to cultivable condition and pay an additional compensation of over RMB 60,000 was clearly unreasonable and was not supported. The original judgment was not erroneous.

Pursuant to Article 151, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the Tianjin High People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 30, 1986: The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. Court acceptance fee of RMB 580.81 for the second instance shall be borne by the appellant.
